name: JPMorgan Chase
description: JPMorgan Chase is the largest US bank and runs four kinds of business under one balance sheet. It takes deposits and lends to about half of American households and to small businesses, and earns most of that income from the gap between what it pays depositors and what it charges on loans and credit cards, plus card and payments fees. Its Commercial & Investment Bank advises companies on deals, underwrites debt and stock, trades bonds, currencies and equities for clients, moves corporate money around the world (payments), and holds assets in custody. Its Asset & Wealth Management arm manages money and runs private banking for wealthy clients for fees. A Corporate unit holds treasury and investment portfolios. Roughly half of total revenue in 2025 came from interest ($95.4B of $182.4B reported net revenue) and the rest from fees, trading and other income.

businessLines.name: Consumer & Community Banking (Chase)
businessLines.shareBasis: of the four segments' total managed net revenue of $185,581M (segments plus Corporate, before reconciling items of -$3,134M)
businessLines.how: Households and small businesses leave deposits that cost the bank little, which it lends out at higher rates (net interest income was $58.2B of the $76.0B); the rest is card interchange and fees, mortgage fees and auto lease income. Credit losses on cards are the main swing factor.
businessLines.description: Banking & Wealth Management, Home Lending, and Card Services & Auto.

businessLines.name: Commercial & Investment Bank
businessLines.how: Fees on advising and underwriting deals, fees and deposit balances on corporate payments and cash management, spreads on loans, and trading and financing revenue from institutional clients; custody fees in Securities Services. Deal fees and trading swing with market activity while payments is steadier.
businessLines.description: Banking & Payments (investment banking, treasury and payments, lending) and Markets & Securities Services (fixed income, equities, securities services).

businessLines.name: Asset & Wealth Management
businessLines.how: Fees charged as a percentage of client assets managed or advised, plus lending and deposit spreads on private-bank clients.
businessLines.description: Investment management and private banking for institutions and wealthy individuals.

businessLines.name: Corporate
businessLines.how: Not a customer business; earns investment yield on the securities portfolio funded by surplus deposits.
businessLines.description: Treasury and Chief Investment Office, other central items.
